# SIDEREAL OBSERVATIONS

you encounter a crowd. Furthermore (which is even more wonderful), the stars called **nebulae** <note>original: "NEBVLOSAE"</note> by every astronomer up to this day are in fact groups of stars planted together in a marvelous way. Although each individual star escapes the sharpest vision due to its smallness or its great distance from us, that whiteness arises from the blending of their rays. This glow was previously believed to be a denser part of the heavens, capable of reflecting the rays of the stars or the Sun. We have observed several of these, and we wished to include diagrams of two such **asterisms** <gloss>star patterns or clusters</gloss>.

In the first diagram, you have what is called the **nebula** <gloss>cloudy patch</gloss> of the Head of Orion, in which we have counted twenty-one stars.

The second contains the **nebula** named **Praesepe** <gloss>the Manger</gloss>. This is not merely one single star, but a mass of more than forty small stars. Besides the **Aselli** <note>original: "Asellos" (the Little Asses), referring to the stars Gamma and Delta Cancri</note>, we have noted thirty-six stars arranged in the following order.

<column-break/>

->THE PRAESEPE NEBULA<-

<note>A telescopic star chart of the Praesepe nebula, now known as the Beehive Cluster. The diagram depicts over thirty-six individual stars, including the two larger stars known as the Aselli, demonstrating how the telescope resolves a cloudy patch into distinct celestial bodies.</note>

->THE ORION NEBULA<-

<note>A telescopic star chart titled the Nebula of Orion. It shows the region around the head of the constellation Orion, revealing twenty-one individual stars that appear as a single hazy spot to the naked eye.</note>

<summary>Galileo explains that astronomical nebulae are actually dense clusters of stars that appear as clouds due to their distance. He provides star charts of the Orion nebula and the Praesepe cluster as visual evidence of his telescopic discoveries.</summary>
<keywords>nebulae, Orion, Praesepe, Beehive Cluster, Aselli, star charts, Sidereus Nuncius, telescopic observation</keywords>
